title: Model orbit activation: catalog-to-announcement GTM checklist
creator: Priya Nair
description: This ticket captures a prescriptive, cross-team checklist to take a newly onboarded model from catalog entry through internal readiness gates to public announcement. Focus areas: accurate catalog metadata, benchmark validation (latency, cost, quality), docs & SDK examples, console surface updates, release notes, and coordinated comms. The goal is a repeatable runway that reduces last-minute blockers and aligns Engineering, Research, Design, Support, and GTM.
checklist: Catalog metadata: canonical name, aliases, tokenizer, model size, recommended sequence length, compatible runtimes
Model compatibility matrix: supported APIs (generation/chat/embeddings/reranking), recommended quantization profiles
Performance baseline: p50/p95 latency on hosted runtime, throughput (tokens/s) on Dedicated tiers
Cost & economics: estimated tokens/second cost, suggested tier mapping (free/paid/dedicated)
Quality benchmarks: eval suites (safety, instruction-following, hallucination rate) and pass thresholds
Open model attribution: license, provenance notes, and any usage restrictions
Docs: quickstart snippets (REST + SDK), parameter guidance, best-practice prompts, caveats
Console & catalog UX: model card, benchmark badges, sample prompts, release tag and changelog
SDK & samples: language-specific example apps, pinned dependency matrix, CI smoke tests
Observability hooks: default dashboards, important traces, common error signatures to monitor
Rollout plan: internal canary -> beta customers -> GA; gate criteria for each stage
Release notes: user-facing summary, breaking changes, migration notes, known limitations
Support readiness: triage playbook, FAQs, escalation matrix, training session scheduled
Compliance & security signoff: KMS/HSM compatibility notes, data residency considerations
Marketing & comms: messaging doc, launch assets, blog draft owner, date for announcement
Post-launch evals: prompt set for regression testing and SLO drift monitoring
comms_plan: Internal launch brief (one-pager) delivered to All-Eng and All-Product two business days before canary
Beta cohort email with instructions and feedback form; Support on-call assigned for first 72 hours
Public launch blog post + changelog entry + API playground update on GA date
Release notes: short bullet list for console header and expanded doc page with migration examples
Social/Partner comms: one-line partner brief + suggested customer outreach snippets
benchmarks_and_metrics: Latency: p50=38ms, p95=120ms on hosted-api small batch (seq len=128)
Throughput: 145 tokens/s per GPU on Dedicated standard profile
Cost baseline: $0.0009 per token-equivalent for generation in hosted tier
Quality: instruction-following accuracy 88% on internal eval set; hallucination rate 3.5%
Regression gates: any change >5% drop in quality or >20% increase in p95 latency blocks GA
rollout_schedule: 2026-03-16: Engineering smoke tests complete and baseline dashboards populated
2026-03-18: Internal canary (team-only) enabled; support on-call monitoring
2026-03-24: Beta cohort (selected customers) + feedback window open (7 days)
2026-03-31: Final signoffs (Research, Security, Docs) and freeze of release assets
2026-04-01: GA / public announcement and blog post publication
risks_mitigation: Risk: Late benchmark regressions — Mitigation: block GA if regression gates are tripped; schedule hotfix sprint
Risk: Docs lag behind engineering changes — Mitigation: put Docs on the critical path; freeze doc owner signoff one week before GA
Risk: Capacity shortage on Dedicated during beta — Mitigation: reserve burst capacity and run load tests against reserved pools
Risk: Messaging misalignment — Mitigation: run pre-announce tabletop with Marketing, Legal, and Product to finalize copy
